scope: REQUIREMENTS.md Part A §10-13: pi-review round cap and stall watchdog, pi-worker, skills contract, the repo test runner (packages/nana-pack, scripts/test.mjs) — 24 off-form origins
notes: ASTRA R1 FIX ROUND (BLOCK 5/10 -> this revision). astra r1's key finding, applied throughout: 'a recorded red mutation proves sensitivity to that mutation; it does not establish coverage of every condition or outcome in the row' — so every implemented clause below was re-checked by mutating EACH condition/outcome its own text names, not just the one mutation that happened to work. MUST 1 (reject all three merges): R-711, R-718 and R-727 are now split, each confirmed by an EXECUTED counterexample that leaves one promise green while the other reds (not just asserted): R-711 — mtime-in-dirty-hash breaks 'revert the edit' while 're-reviewing an already-counted revision' and 'worktree W2...' stay green (both clean-commit scenarios, untouched by a dirty-hash mutation); R-718 — forcing `mine=false` breaks only 'complete(B) recorded...' (own-a-live-reservation) while the three invalid-reservation refusals are already correct regardless; R-727 — wrong exit code (0) breaks only the status half of the one cited test while 'running the watchdog first' (astra's own technique) breaks only its never-runs half, confirming the merge hid two independently-breakable facts. MUST 2 (restore the directory-lock-path refusal): new R-852 restores 'a directory lock path shall be refused at once with a message and no stack, before the review runs' as its own row (R-723 stays the general 'every ledger path shall be a regular file'; R-844 is reworded to drop the unproven 'at once' for the symlink/unwritable-directory cases specifically, since astra's 4-second-delay counterexample showed neither of those two citations checks timing). MUST 3 (six PARTIAL rows): R-833 downgraded to untested (no assertion pins preservation of the literal --revision value, only acceptance); R-843 split so 'naming file and line' is claimed only for the malformed/corrupted case (the only one the citation proves), with incomplete-record refusal split into its own row, R-853, without that unproven guarantee; R-844 — see MUST 2; R-846 downgraded to untested (its only citation launches pi-worker, a neighbouring case, not pi-review); R-910 gains a second, dual-tagged citation (the existing non-zero-exit assertion) plus its own new mutation, since the original citation covered only the exit-0-plus-FAIL-line half; R-912 narrowed to the timeout trigger only (dual-citing R-609's own process-tree-kill evidence), with the Ctrl-C/SIGTERM trigger split into new R-915, untested — astra's counterexample (clearing active/ scratch at the top of the signal handler) leaves the entire 24-check file green, confirming no test sends a signal to the runner. SHOULD (standalone sentences): R-842, R-845, R-846, R-847, R-849, R-911, R-912, R-913, R-914 reworded to name their own subject/condition instead of a sibling-dependent pronoun or elliptical opener. NOTE corrections: R-831's recorded mutation is unchanged (renaming the default predicate to the literal name `reviewShaped` hits both the import-regex and the name-regex at once) but its EXPLANATION was wrong to claim this isolates the import promise cleanly; a cleaner, independently-verified alternative (importing `canonicalItem` from review-round.mjs — a real import matching the import-regex but containing no occurrence of the literal name `reviewShaped`) is now the recorded mutation, confirmed red and genuinely isolating R-831 from R-702. R-911's mutation is corrected per astra's NOTE: the original (`f === 0` added to `ok`) also suppressed the WARN push (`if (ok && f)` requires `ok`), so it did not isolate 'shall not flip the verdict' from R-606's 'reported as a WARN'; the new mutation touches only the LABEL computation, confirmed to leave the WARN line intact. Isolated-reproduction scripts for R-723/R-852, R-837 and R-721 (plus one for R-718, not explicitly requested but written on the same ground: forcing `mine=false` to isolate 'own a live reservation' is too destructive to run against the full file) are committed at docs/reviews/ears-form-2026-10-04/isolated-repro-{r723,r837,r721,r718}.mjs, each run standalone at both baseline (PASS) and under its mutation (FAIL) before being recorded here. R-723/R-852's script carries NO added timeout — astra r1 SHOULD corrected this worker's earlier, wrong claim that the cited call hangs forever; it fails correctly via ledgerRun's own existing 30000ms spawnSync timeout, confirmed at ~31s against the REAL file (not a substitute) before the isolated script was written for fast iteration. R-721's script keeps both conjuncts of the real assertion (absence of .1 AND three retained rounds), not just the first. R-837's script discloses its one necessary adaptation (guarding the cleanup unlink so the script itself can still report a result when the mutation has already removed the lock). Sibling-cite list (6), all legitimate: R-831 (see NOTE correction above) and R-911 (see NOTE correction above) and R-914 (shares R-615's two cites — R-615's mutation drops a fixture, wrong COUNT; R-914's mutation misdeclares one fixture's expected verdict, wrong MATCH; both confirmed independently red) each use TWO DIFFERENT mutations hitting two different disjuncts/branches of one compound boolean. R-852 shares R-723's one cite AND mutation (the lock-dir isFile-check removal) deliberately, on the A2 R-142/R-828 precedent ('shared citations are allowed where the implementation genuinely renders both facts in one literal'): removing that ONE check is the ONLY code path that makes a lock-directory simultaneously (a) not a regular file (R-723) and (b) refused late/silently/without-message (R-852's four guarantees) — these are not two separately-achievable code states, so one mutation legitimately pins both rows. R-854 likewise shares R-727's cite AND mutation by design (see R-854's own `assertion` text: astra r1's counterexample distinguished only 'refused' from 'never runs', never 'no worker mode' from 'refused' — no separate mutation exists to invent). R-851 shares the same cite as R-727/R-854 but with its OWN, different mutation (running the watchdog before refusing), confirmed to leave R-727/R-854's exit-code half intact.
